question.text: Two coherent monochromatic point sources S1 and S2 of wavelength λ=600nm are placed symmetrically on either side of the center of the circle as shown. The sources are separated by a distance d=1.8 mm. This arrangement produces interference fringes visible as alternate bright and dark spots on the circumference of the circle. The angular separation between two consecutive bright spots is Δθ . Which of the following options is/are correct?

options.text: A dark spot will be formed at the point  <math><msub><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>

The angular separation between two consecutive bright spots decreases as we move from  <math><msub><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>  to  <math><msub><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  along the first quadrant
At <math><msub><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> the order of the fringe will be maximum

The total number of fringes produced between <math><msub><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> in the first quadrant is close to 3000

solution.text:
At point P2;

Δx=d=1.8 mm=3000 λ

Hence a (bright fringe) will be formed at P2

Now   Δx=d cos⁡θ=nλ

cos⁡θ=nλd, θ is with the x-axis.

-sinθ Δθ=Δnλd

Δθ=-Δn λd sin⁡θ

Δθ increases as θ decreases

At   P2,  the order of fringe will be maximum.

For total no. of bright fringes d=nλ  ⇒  n=3000

∴   total no. of fringes =3000
